- **Color pattern:** Asymmetric blotchy yellowing (chlorosis) — the left/lower portion of the leaf shows distinct yellow-green to yellow patches while the right/upper portion remains more green
- **Pattern type:** Irregular, blotchy, asymmetric mottling — the yellow areas don't follow a uniform pattern and appear on one side of the midrib more than the other

**Reasoning:**

- **Huanglongbing (HLB / Citrus Greening):** This disease is characterized by asymmetric, blotchy mottling on citrus leaves — the yellowing/chlorosis is typically patchy and asymmetric across the leaf midrib, appearing on citrus. The image shows a citrus-type leaf with exactly this kind of irregular, asymmetric yellow blotching pattern on an otherwise green leaf.

- **Whisker Mold:** This typically presents as fuzzy/hairy mold growth (usually white, gray, or black mycelial growth) on plant surfaces — no such fungal structures are visible here.

The asymmetric, blotchy chlorotic mottling on what appears to be a citrus leaf is the hallmark symptom of Huanglongbing.
